page: Amazon Web Services c6i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 virtual CPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading. Hardware instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI support), AES-NI, and SHA-NI for cryptographic efficiency. Memory resources total 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Dedicated acceleration hardware is not included, with 0 GPUs attached. High core density allows strong multi-threaded capabilities, though workloads requiring massive memory per thread or local NVMe scratch storage must account for the platform constraints.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong tier placement in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core (61,949.65), PassMark CPU score (57,907.19), Clang software compilation (40,600.0), and Geekbench ray tracing (57,444.0). Cryptographic and vector extension workloads show elevated throughput, supported by PassMark CPU extended instructions (54,525.71) and encryption tests (56,892.24). Single-core benchmark measurements, such as Geekbench single-core (1,691.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,893.7), align within average tier bands.

In memory and operational tests, memory bandwidth achieved 166.09 GB/sec read and 66.04 GB/sec write on uncached blocks. In application scenarios, PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput (44.87 GB/sec) placed in the upper quartile, alongside text generation on small and medium LLM inference models. The instance delivers high compute density per dollar for CPU-bound pipelines, making it suited for distributed compilation, high-concurrency web serving, batch data transformation, and compute-intensive database backends.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It integrates 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory configured at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPUs. Performance testing shows strong results in multi-core compute tests, including PassMark CPU tests, software compilation, static web serving throughput, and multi-threaded decompression, while single-core processing and raw memory bandwidth perform within average bands. With AVX-512 VNNI support and dense multi-threaded compute, the instance is well suited for CPU-bound workloads such as large-scale software builds, batch processing, static web fleets, and distributed data transformation.
